title: Eileen Gray's birth chart
metaDescription: Eileen Gray's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.8° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 15.8° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 15.8° Leo — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 12.5° Virgo, Venus was at 15.8° Cancer, Mars was at 29.3° Leo. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars in the same degree of the zodiac from Uranus, 0.3° off exact. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Saturn at 1.9°, and Uranus square Pluto at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. The Sun in Leo at 15.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Virgo at 12.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Aries at 2.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 5 fire, 3 earth, 1 water, 1 air by element and 6 fixed, 2 mutable, 2 cardinal by mode. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 23.2°.
